explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration matching this theorem. It describes how a torus element acts by conjugation on the F4 short-root adjoint matrices over an 𝔽₂-algebra. Every constant in the statement is the library's own: f4ShortRootWeightTorusGL, f4ShortRootAdjointMatrixBaseChange, f4ShortRootQuotientLift, torusCharacter and f4ShortRootQuotientWeight. I worked this out from the statement and the proof shown, without running any searches. Mathlib has no F4-specific Lie algebra objects, which is why I did not search it. The proof splits into two cases and in each one applies the library's own lemmas: f4ShortRootWeightTorusGL_conj_root for roots and f4ShortRootWeightTorusGL_conj_simpleCoroot for coroots. The Mathlib lemmas it uses (Matrix.lieConj_apply, Units.val_one, one_smul) are generic simp lemmas and don't count as a match. The mathematical content lies in the library's own definitions.
